Protein Food

Beef Brisket

About This Entry

Brisket is a tough, collagen-rich chest cut that becomes tender and unctuous after long slow cooking. Smoked or braised brisket's fat, smoke, and umami call for reds with depth — often Syrah, Zinfandel, or softer tannin after long cook times.

Beginner Guide

Brisket has two layers: the leaner flat and the fattier point (deckle). BBQ brisket is almost always slow-smoked; braised brisket appears in Jewish and Central European traditions.

FAQ

What is Beef Brisket?
Brisket has two layers: the leaner flat and the fattier point (deckle).
How should Beef Brisket be cooked for best results?
Rich cuts tolerate medium to medium-rare; render fat slowly on roasts and braises. Rest before serving so juices redistribute.
